# Sum of balls, one-limb center, finite core

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_add_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x + y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call [`ball_add_1_full`](ball_add_1_full.md), which computes this kernel and then the fix-up of its results.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $r_x \ge 0$.
- $r_y \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $\lvert (x + y) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_add_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball2.v), against `ball_add_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_add_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx rx cy ry : R,
  fmt emin prec cx ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec cy ->
  fmt emin prec ry ->
  0 <= rx ->
  0 <= ry ->
  let '(cz, rz) := ball_add_1 emin prec tie_even cx rx cy ry in
  fmt emin prec cz /\
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  (forall x y : R, Rabs (x - cx) <= rx -> Rabs (y - cy) <= ry -> Rabs ((x + y) - cz) <= rz).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius sum (Milestone 1 listing, second radius design). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_add_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_add_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The sum of two balls with one-limb centers: the center by one operation of T, the radius in the second design.
# The radius is evaluated by operations rounded to nearest on nonnegative values and inflated
# once (milestone1.md, "The radius, second design"): E turns the error bound of the center
# kernel add_1_1 into a multiple of |cz0|, G covers the roundings of the radius, H what underflow
# loses and the absolute term of the bound. Each is an exact expression rounded up. H also
# contains eta/(2u), the smallest normal number, which no bound needs: it makes H, and with it
# every radius a kernel returns, a normal number, because a fused operation with a subnormal
# operand is slow on some processors (decisions.md, the log of 2026-11-19).

cz = add(cx, cy)
az = abs(cz)
s  = add(rx, ry)
t  = fma(az, const up(unit(add_1_1)/(1-unit(add_1_1))), s)
rz = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_add_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 958 848 | 0 | 1.25 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 874 584 | 0 | 1.25 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 20 935 808 | 0 | 1.03125 (`fp:3:-4:2`) |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_add_1_full`](ball_add_1_full.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
